Simon Evans' revival of A Day in the Death of Joe Egg is a fitting memorial tribute.

So although Simon Evans's production often feels dated, it is still full of the bravery with which the play made its mark - from tackling a subject that was once taboo, to placing a disabled character (affectingly played by Toolis, who has cerebral palsy) centre stage.

cn.t: Nichols' groundbreaking 1967 play remains powerful and provocative, though some find this revival listless or dated. Stephens earns praise for his bravura performance, but the production doesn't fully deliver on the script's firecracker potential.
